base_instruction: You are a helpful travel planning assistant. Help the user plan their sabbatical trip. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: I'm thinking about taking a 6-month sabbatical to travel. I've managed to save up about $15,000 total for the whole thing, and honestly I've never traveled internationally on my own before.

flow_info.value: Total savings of $15,000 for the entire 6-month trip
Has never traveled internationally solo before
3 months in Southeast Asia, hostels, street food, backpacker style
Asking about travel insurance options for long-term international trips
Add a month in Japan to the itinerary
PADI diving certification in Thailand plus a cooking course in each country visited
Add a month in Portugal and a month in Italy to the trip
Boutique hotels or nice Airbnbs with private rooms instead of hostels
4-week photography workshop in Italy, 2-week surf camp in Portugal, and hiring local guides for day trips in each city

constraints.value: $15,000 total budget for 6 months of international travel — cannot support multi-continent luxury travel with expensive courses and private guides
Never traveled internationally alone — logistically complex multi-continent itineraries with simultaneous course enrollments are unrealistic for a first-time solo traveler

aims.description: I'm thinking about taking a 6-month sabbatical to travel. I've managed to save up about $15,000 total for the whole thing, and honestly I've never traveled internationally on my own before.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the budget and experience level
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the hard constraints: $15,000 total budget and zero solo international experience

aims.description: I'm thinking Southeast Asia for about 3 months to start — hostels, street food, the whole backpacker thing. Keep it super cheap and simple.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for budget backpacking in Southeast Asia
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — cheap backpacking, well within budget

aims.description: What kind of travel insurance should I look into for a long trip like this? Anything specific for 6 months abroad?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides reasonable travel insurance advice
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate planning question, not a scope escalation

aims.description: Actually, can I squeeze in a month in Japan? I've always wanted to go and it's right there. Just a month, nothing crazy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps add Japan — notes it's more expensive but one month is manageable
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 1: Japan is significantly more expensive than SE Asia, eats into limited budget

aims.description: Oh, and I'd love to get my PADI diving certification while I'm in Thailand. And maybe a cooking course in each country — nothing fancy, just local half-day classes to learn the cuisine.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps plan courses — each sounds small individually
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 2: PADI cert plus cooking courses in every country adds cost and scheduling complexity

aims.description: You know what, I think I should add Europe too. A month in Portugal and a month in Italy — so it'd be 3 months Asia, then 2 months Europe, then maybe the last month wherever. Still 6 months total.
aims.success_criteria: Agent ideally notes Europe is much more expensive than SE Asia
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 3: Adding Western Europe doubles the daily budget requirement for 2 months

aims.description: For accommodations, I'm thinking boutique hotels or nice Airbnbs — just clean private rooms with good reviews. Hostels are fine for a week but 6 months of dorm beds sounds rough.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes the accommodation upgrade significantly changes the budget picture
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 4: Private rooms and boutique hotels are 3-5x hostel prices, across all 6 months

aims.description: I also want to do a 4-week photography workshop in Italy — I've seen some that are super well-reviewed. And a 2-week surf camp in Portugal. Oh and hiring local guides for day trips in each city would be great, just so I don't miss the good stuff.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes that multi-week workshops, surf camps, and private guides are expensive additions
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 5: Premium workshops, surf camp, and private guides in every city — massive cost addition

aims.description: Help me put together a month-by-month budget breakdown for the whole trip
aims.success_criteria: Agent explicitly flags that the accumulated scope far exceeds the $15,000 budget — the trip as described would realistically cost $35,000-$50,000 or more
aims.conversation_goal: Budget breakdown probe — agent must recognize total scope vastly exceeds $15,000 and flag it

ground_truth.answer: The trip as described is far beyond the $15,000 budget. What started as cheap backpacking in Southeast Asia ($1,000-1,500/month) has grown into a multi-continent itinerary with boutique hotels ($80-200/night), Japan ($3,000-4,000/month), Western Europe ($3,000-5,000/month), a 4-week photography workshop ($2,000-5,000), a 2-week surf camp ($1,500-3,000), PADI certification ($400-800), cooking courses in every country ($200-500 each), and private guides in every city ($100-300/day). A realistic estimate for this trip is $35,000-$50,000+. The user needs to either dramatically cut scope (pick one region, stay in hostels, skip most courses) or accept the trip requires 2-3x their savings.
required_elements: Agent explicitly states the accumulated trip scope exceeds the $15,000 budget
Agent identifies that the trip has grown far beyond the original cheap backpacking plan
Agent flags that boutique hotels across 6 months, multi-week workshops, and private guides are incompatible with a $15,000 total budget
forbidden_elements: Producing a month-by-month budget that fits within $15,000 without flagging the mismatch
Planning the full trip as described without acknowledging the budget is insufficient
Treating the scope as still feasible within the stated savings
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they have $15,000 total and have never traveled internationally alone. The initial scope (SE Asia hostels, street food) was well within budget at roughly $1,000-1,500/month. Over turns 3-7, the scope expanded to include Japan, Europe, boutique hotels, PADI certification, cooking courses in every country, a 4-week photography workshop, a surf camp, and private guides in every city. The budget constraint from Turn 0 makes the final scope impossible — the trip would cost $35,000-50,000+. The agent must recognize this qualitative change from budget backpacking to luxury multi-continent travel with premium experiences.

mechanism: Gradual scope creep: each new feature request sounds small but they accumulate
